title: Skipping class and the cigar lesson from his father
summary: After he and Maceo Mayfield hook school to smoke, his father gives him cigars and he never smokes cigarettes again.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So, okay, so we're in Philadelphia and you're playing these rent parties and this is around, what? 1914, still?

I want to tell you an incident that happened, this was about -- I was just goin' to the high school, now let's see, that must have been '15, or '14 or '15. Anyhow, it was in there somewhere. Anyhow, we'd just started to smoke. Because we had been goin' to rent parties, and I had had a little taste of liquor, but, blackberry and gin we used to go for, see. We thought that really helped you, sexually. We went for that strongly, see we thought that would give you the kick that you needed to please the little girls.
So we, as we were goin' up the street, we had two cigarettes that we had hooked in school. I had

started to hook in school, now. That we'd hooked in school, and we were goin' up the street and all of a sudden, Mayfield said to me, he said, "Jesus, there comes your father. There's your old man down the street." Well, we nearly choked these cigarettes, we choked them right quick and we put them in our pockets. And he come on down there, and he said, "Hiya boys, where you all goin'?" And we said, "Oh, we didn't have any class, so we were goin' up to -- up on Market Street to the Nickelle." Well, we did have a class, but we had hooked it. We had jumped the class. Anyhow, so we lied about it and he said, "Alright, go ahead, but don't get into any trouble." He went on about his business and we kept on goin'. Well, I told Maceo Mayfield, "I'm very happy that we got in, and he didn't see us smokin' those cigarettes." Because he'd always told me, "Well, now look (unintelligible), if you're going to be an athlete, you can't be smokin'. And goin' on like that, see, so I was very happy. I got home that night. We had supper, and I was smug in as a rug. I thought I had fooled him. Well, he reached into his pocket and took two Cinco cigars out. And said, well, he called me David, that's my middle name, he said, "Listen, David," he said, "I see you're goin' to smoke, anyhow. So, if you're goin' to smoke, smoke cigars. Don't smoke cigarettes, they're bad for your lungs and all of that." Don't you know, I've never smoked a cigarette since that day.
But, it was not the thought of the cigarette, but the thought that I'd fooled him, and I hadn't fooled him.
